name: Sunburst
summary: Rays from a disc or a half disc: a sign of light and of the new, on a facade, a gate, a mirror or a clock.
how: Draw 12 to 36 rays from one centre; alternate long and short rays, or two finishes.
Keep the centre disc at 15% to 30% of the full diameter.
In a room, use one sunburst as the focal point of one wall.

origin.note: Rays from a half disc appear on Art Deco facades, gates and lift doors around the Paris exposition of decorative arts in 1925.

adoptions.via: Mirrors, clocks, grilles and lamps of the Paris exposition of decorative arts carry rays from a half disc in gilt brass and glass.
Art Deco furniture, screens and mirrors take the ray motif inside.
Clarice Cliff paints rays and bands of flat colour on Bizarre ware.
Hollywood decorators hang sunburst mirrors and starburst lights in the homes and sets of film stars.
George Nelson Associates design ray-form wall clocks for Howard Miller; the starburst mirror follows in the 1950s.
Space Age signs, packaging and posters use starbursts as a sign of the future.
Neo-deco rooms bring back the fan and the sunburst in brass and glass.

sources.title: Bevis Hillier, Art Deco of the 20s and 30s (Studio Vista, 1968)
